source.title: Towards Robust and Parameter-Efficient Knowledge Unlearning for LLMs
source.authors: Sungmin Cha; Sungjun Cho; Dasol Hwang; Moontae Lee

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures targeted-data forgetting and retained capabilities using extraction and memorization metrics, but does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated examples, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt changes. Its unlearning-success criterion compares EL10 and MA on the forget set with values on unseen validation data; it does not report recovery under attacks or establish chance-level performance.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It proposes LoKU (IHL plus FILA) and reports only its own and baseline methods' forgetting metrics (EL10/MA on TDEC, TOFU forget quality) and utility. No relearning, activation-ablation, quantization or prompting attack is run, so its results cannot show whether unlearning is shallow or deep. The success criterion is 'below unseen-validation EL10/MA', a surface-output threshold, not a robustness test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that LoKU gives faster, more stable LoRA-based unlearning with better post-unlearning utility than GA/GD and other baselines. They make no claim about recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a different unlearning objective and adapter initialization; it does not reproduce the attack or recovery procedures in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Unlearning success and post-unlearning performance vary with the unlearning method, LoRA rank, adapted modules, and forget-set size; the paper reports failures for some settings.

fits_no_version.finding: TOFU: FILA can over-unlearn (forget quality falls after peaking, e.g. Llama2-7B forget10 at ranks 8/16). The authors liken this to a Streisand effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-unlearning can make the forget set more distinguishable from a retain-only reference model.

record.problems: The reported success criterion compares forget-set EL10 and MA with unseen-validation values rather than chance. Recovery attacks are not tested. The prose gives no numerical aggregate success rates for the Figure 3 results.
record.rows_left_out: No recovery-attack results are reported. Detailed TOFU evaluations and other downstream-capability measurements are not separately catalogued here because they do not test recovery after unlearning.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the forgotten content. Chance-level accuracy is not the criterion; only below-validation EL10/MA and TOFU forget quality are used.
Activation-direction ablation, or analysis of blocking vs deletion.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context recovery.
No claim or test of resistance to recovery attacks. 'Robust' in the title refers to optimization stability.

record.verdict_notes: In the title, 'Robust' means stable optimization, not resistance to recovery attacks, so this is not a version-F study. All rows are method comparisons and are relinked to none. The record's limits_scope label on A is dropped, because the study never tests the attack part of A, and surface forgetting metrics alone cannot bear on whether unlearning is shallow.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge; whether targeted accuracy reaches chance specifically. The study uses its own validation-set forgetting criterion.
Fine-tuning after unlearning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
Ablating activation directions or testing whether the methods block access rather than delete knowledge.
Recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Resistance of a newer method to the recovery attacks above.

rows.subject: GPT-Neo 125M, 1.3B, and 2.7B (aggregate statement)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient Difference (GD) with LoRA for unlearning TDEC sequences

conditions.value: varied in Figure 3; not stated for the aggregate claim

rows.measure: Whether EL10 and Memorization Accuracy on the forget set meet the paper's unlearning criterion
rows.baseline: EL10 and MA on an unseen validation set; numeric values not stated here
rows.value: The paper states that GD with LoRA fails to unlearn effectively across all model sizes; Figure 3 includes multiple unsuccessful attempts.
rows.note: Aggregate statement about the GPT-Neo family; the paper's criterion is below unseen-validation values, not a stated chance level.
rows.check: This is a baseline comparison (GD+LoRA vs the study's own method), not a test of any version. The value is also misread. Table 1 shows GD with rank-16 LoRA meeting the criterion (e.g. 8.6 epochs on 125M). The failures are some trials in Figure 3, not 'across all model sizes' in every case.

rows.subject: GPT-Neo 125M, 1.3B, and 2.7B (aggregate statement)
rows.operation_detail: Replacing the GA loss term in GD with Inverted Hinge Loss (IHL), with LoRA

conditions.value: varied in Figure 3; not stated for the aggregate claim

rows.measure: Whether EL10 and Memorization Accuracy on the forget set meet the paper's unlearning criterion
rows.baseline: GD with LoRA; unseen-validation EL10 and MA thresholds
rows.value: IHL improves performance, but the paper states that it still fails to unlearn in multiple cases.
rows.note: The text describes failures across trials but does not give a numerical failure count in this passage.
rows.check: This compares the study's own IHL component against a baseline. It measures forgetting under the authors' criterion, not recovery after unlearning.

rows.subject: GPT-Neo 125M, 1.3B, and 2.7B (aggregate statement)
rows.operation_detail: GD with Fisher-Initialization of Low-rank Adapters (FILA)

conditions.value: varied in Figure 3; not stated for the aggregate claim

rows.measure: Unlearning success rate under the paper's EL10 and Memorization Accuracy criterion, and downstream capability performance
rows.baseline: GD with LoRA; pretrained-model performance for downstream tasks
rows.value: FILA notably increases the rate of unlearning success, but at significant cost in overall performance in many cases.
rows.note: The text does not report an aggregate numerical success rate.
rows.check: This compares the study's own FILA component with GD. It is a success-rate and utility trade-off, with no attack.

rows.subject: GPT-Neo 125M, 1.3B, and 2.7B (aggregate statement)
rows.operation_detail: LoKU: IHL with FILA-initialized LoRA adapters

conditions.value: varied in Figure 3; not stated for the aggregate claim

rows.measure: Unlearning success under the EL10 and Memorization Accuracy criterion, plus reasoning, dialogue, and Pile perplexity after unlearning
rows.baseline: Unseen-validation EL10 and MA for the unlearning criterion; pretrained-model performance for downstream tasks
rows.value: The paper states that LoKU best minimizes post-unlearning performance degradation across the reported aspects and reduces the number of epochs required for IHL; it does not give a numerical aggregate in this passage.
rows.note: The reported forgetting criterion is not a direct test of chance-level accuracy or resistance to recovery attacks.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's own performance. Surface forgetting metrics without any recovery attack cannot show whether knowledge is removed or hidden.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: TDEC experiments with GPT-Neo models and LoRA
reader_labels.reason: Forgetting outcomes vary: GD with LoRA fails across model sizes, IHL still fails in multiple cases, and FILA with GD trades increased success for performance loss; LoKU improves the reported trade-off, but the study does not establish chance-level accuracy or test attacks (r1–r4).
